sections.title: Architecture and Loading (Parallel Dual-Scan)
sections.content:
Pip Manager is a standalone window opened via double-click or right-click on an environment in the main Manager. It uses an advanced Parallel Dual-Scan algorithm (via ThreadPoolExecutor). In the background, two independent processes run concurrently within the exact same millisecond:

  1. Local Scan: Instantly reads installed packages from disk (list --format=json).
  2. Cloud Scan: Concurrently checks for the latest available versions on PyPI servers (list --outdated --format=json).

The results are merged into a clear, unified table. If the version number is GREEN, you are on the latest release. If it is RED, an update is available.

Support for both Pip and UV: Queries run using whichever package manager is configured in settings. When using the UV installer, loading the package list is nearly instantaneous.

sections.title: Single Package Management and Safety Guards
sections.content:
The right panel is context-sensitive. It activates upon selecting a specific row in the table (e.g. the requests package).

Smart 'Update' Button

  • Update Available: If a newer version is found, the button becomes active with the label: '⬆️ Update to [version]'.
  • Up to Date: If you already have the latest version, the button is disabled and shows: '✅ Version is up to date'.

Protection Against Environment Breakage (APT Guard)

The ❌ Uninstall button protects the integrity of your environment on two levels:

  1. Reverse Dependency Blocking: If you attempt to uninstall a package required by another installed library (or an attached Local Package), VenvHub Pro blocks the operation immediately and informs you which packages still depend on it.
  2. requirements.txt Detection: If a package is explicitly declared in the project's requirements.txt, the application issues a strong warning dialog prior to uninstallation.

Live Birth Certificate Updates

Following every successful install, update, or uninstall operation, the application immediately updates venv_birth_certificate.json in the background.

sections.title: APT Autoremove and Dependency Self-Cleaning
sections.content:
VenvHub Pro features a dependency management engine inspired by the Linux APT (Advanced Package Tool) package management system. This engine runs silently in the background of all operations.

How does APT Autoremove work?

When you install a large package (e.g. pandas), multiple transitive dependencies are downloaded (numpy, pytz, dateutil). In standard Pip, uninstalling Pandas leaves these leftover libraries orphaned indefinitely as bloatware.

Instead, VenvHub Pro automatically:

  1. Analyzes the Dependency Tree: Determines which packages were explicitly requested by you (explicit roots) and which were pulled in as secondary dependencies.
  2. Identifies Orphans: Finds packages that are no longer required by any remaining library.
  3. Cleans the Environment: Safely and automatically removes all orphaned packages, keeping your Venv footprint minimal.

requirements.txt Synchronization ('requirements.txt' Button)

VenvHub Pro tracks package history from previous installations in its internal state database (venvhub_apt_state.json).

When you delete or comment out (#) a line in requirements.txt and subsequently click the requirements.txt button in the app:

  • The application first installs any missing dependencies.
  • At the same time, it detects deleted or commented lines and automatically uninstalls them from the venv alongside their unused dependencies (unless you manually installed that package in the past as a permanent standalone tool).
Self-Healing: Core build tools such as pip, setuptools, wheel, and uv are permanently protected and never removed by the system. Furthermore, if you manually install a package outside VenvHub, the system recognizes it and protects it from removal.

sections.title: Downgrade (Reverting to an Older Version)
sections.content:
Sometimes a newly released package version introduces bugs or breaks compatibility with your code. In such cases, you need to perform a Downgrade.

In the right panel under 'Install specific version':

  1. Look at the 'Installed Version' column (for example 2.5.0).
  2. Enter the lower version number you need into the input field (for example 2.4.0).
  3. Click the Install Version button.

The application triggers an exact version installation in the background (pip install package==2.4.0). The installer automatically replaces the existing version with the requested older release.

sections.title: Bulk Updates and Autopilot (Pip vs UV)
sections.content:
The ⬆️ Update All Outdated button initiates a batch process that upgrades all outdated (red) packages at once. However, behavior differs significantly depending on your chosen package manager:

Standard Manager (Classic Pip)

Standard pip updates packages sequentially. If a dependency collision occurs after updating, it requires manual inspection of logs and troubleshooting.

Ultra-fast Manager (UV - Astral) ✨ Autopilot

If you use uv in Settings, VenvHub Pro executes an Autopilot dependency audit and repair immediately after bulk updating:

  1. Ultra-fast Update: Downloads and installs the latest versions concurrently in parallel.
  2. Integrity Check (uv pip check): Verifies compatibility across the entire environment.
  3. Auto-Fix: If an updated package breaks downstream dependencies, the system parses the error output automatically and forces a corrective downgrade to a compatible version.
  4. Post-update Cleanup: The APT engine audits remaining packages and uninstalls any legacy incompatible orphans.

sections.title: Freeze and Logging
sections.content:
The 📜 Freeze > requirements.txt button exports a package manifest with pinned version numbers directly into your project's root folder.

Asynchronous Execution and Safety Locks

All operations (Freeze, Install, Update, Uninstall) run on a dedicated asynchronous worker thread (QThread), streaming live CLI output directly to the Log window. During any ongoing task, all UI action buttons are temporarily disabled to prevent race conditions within the environment.
